title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and automation tool being used as an active component in a ransomware campaign. The Aurora operators directed Cursor Agent, which runs on Claude Sonnet, to carry out hands-on exploitation tasks against target organizations. The tool was not breached or manipulated into behaving unexpectedly, it was simply operated by attackers as a productivity aid, the same way a legitimate user might. This is a misuse failure, not a model safety failure: the system did what it was designed to do, at the direction of malicious operators.

The point of failure is at access rather than at the model level. No technical safeguard prevented the attackers from subscribing to and directing the tool toward intrusion tasks. The operators even imposed their own operational constraints on the agent, forbidding techniques they considered risky, which shows deliberate, skilled use rather than opportunistic experimentation. Catching this kind of abuse would require monitoring of how the tool is being used, detection of patterns consistent with network reconnaissance or lateral movement, or controls on the categories of commands the agent will execute, none of which are standard features of general-purpose AI coding assistants.

What is not established is whether Cursor or Anthropic had any knowledge of this use before the researchers published their findings, or whether the companies have since taken any action in response.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group has been active since April 2026 and developed a Linux variant designed to target ESXi environments. The group operated a data leak site and targeted organizations across multiple countries. Researchers found that Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations between April 8 and May 21, 2026. The ESXi ransomware encrypts virtual machine files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can read ransom demands, and includes specialized modes for targeting specific environments.

The investigation identified two distinct clusters of Aurora activity. The first cluster used custom tools like esxi_finder.py to locate ESXi hosts and vCenter servers on victim networks, then deployed the ransomware via manual copying. Operators placed strict restrictions on the AI agent, forbidding certain techniques like DCSync attacks and account lockouts. A second Aurora cluster, attributed with medium confidence to potentially different operators, used different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and S3 data exfiltration across eight victim organizations in six countries.
